# Wen Almanac

> An open, community-maintained, fact-checked record of Wen — the cat on Solana that began as a poem and grew into an open NFT standard (WNS) — kept as history and usefulness: no prices, no forecasts, no exchange links. Every claim links to a source; every source is on one page.

Last updated: 2026-10-20. Language: English. Not the official Wen site (official: https://wenwencoin.com/). Not financial advice.

## How to read this almanac (reading model)

1. **Identity.** Wen is a Solana token whose supply is a poem: Meow, co-founder of Jupiter, wrote "A Love Letter to Wen Bros"; it was minted as an NFT and split into 1,000,000,000,000 tokens. The one real WEN is the Solana mint `WENWENvqqNya429ubCdR81ZmD69brwQaaBYY6p3LCpk`. Names, logos and tickers can be copied; the address cannot.
2. **History.** WNS 0.0 was proposed on January 25, 2024 on the Jupiter Research forum. WEN launched on January 26, 2024 as the first token of Jupiter's LFG Launchpad and was airdropped to more than one million wallets (643,652 WEN per eligible wallet) — a live stress test that Solana passed. When the claim closed on January 29, 2024, the unclaimed allocation — over 271 billion WEN, about 27.2% of supply — was burned.
3. **Technology.** The Wen New Standard (WNS) builds light NFTs on Solana's Token-2022: metadata in the mint, group/member pointers for collections, and a transfer hook that enforces creator royalties. The code is open in the Wen Program Library (https://github.com/wen-community/wen-program-library).
4. **Usefulness.** Wen Open Lab turns WNS and Token-2022 into free, tested models — receipts and warranty cards, creator royalties, B2B invoices, a payments bridge, a card-versus-on-chain payment simulator — with a devnet run anyone can repeat. Lab code is educational and not audited.
5. **Trust.** Each claim is marked verified, reported (announced by the official X account) or unverified in the trust chain. Every external link is on the sources page. Posts carry a badge: Historical post, Reworked market post or Almanac guide.
6. **Safety.** Search the address, not the name. No real team, airdrop or support chat ever needs a seed phrase. Test on devnet with a new, empty wallet.

When citing this almanac, link the specific page and, for facts, the source card on https://wen-watt.github.io/sources.html.

## How Wen's usefulness connects people, machines, robots and calculation systems

This is the almanac's own reading of the record, built only from the verified facts above.

- **People.** The poem, the cat and the community art make an open door into how a token works; the quiz (250 checked questions) and the safety rules teach verification habits: check the address, keep the seed phrase private, read the source.
- **Machines.** WNS moves rules into the token itself (Token-2022 extensions): metadata, collections and royalties are enforced by programs, not by the goodwill of each app. A rule that lives in the token works the same in every wallet and marketplace.
- **Robots and agents.** Machine-readable proofs travel with the token: a soulbound receipt or warranty card (Non-Transferable), an invoice whose terms the token enforces, a payment request a program can read (Solana Pay). Automated agents can check these on-chain without trusting a screenshot.
- **Calculation systems.** Supply, authorities and burns are public data on the Solana ledger; anyone can recompute them on an explorer. The Lab's payment simulator compares card and on-chain fees with open formulas; its devnet run is reproducible.
- **The pool of links.** People learn from the story, machines enforce the rules, agents read the proofs, ledgers keep the numbers — and every link points back to a source that a human can check. That loop is the usefulness the almanac records.
